sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and purpose
sections.what: Imports the database, the demo pin checks and the sample helpers, and states what the test proves.
sections.why: Explains the goals to a reader before the checks start.
sections.watch_out: The server address comes from an environment variable, so the test points nowhere if it is missing.

sections.name: json
sections.title: Fetch helper
sections.what: Requests a URL and fails the test unless the response status is 200, then returns the body as data.
sections.why: Keeps each request check short and fails loudly on a bad status.
sections.watch_out: Only the status is checked here, so an error hidden in the body is not caught by this helper.

sections.name: writeFingerprint (part 1)
sections.title: Snapshot and pin checks
sections.what: Reads row counts and content hashes for the main tables, then checks the pins, the LNG project list, the evidence example and the hints for banned text. Also prepares the export request.
sections.why: Reason for the name not stated in the code. The function only reads the database and does not write to it.
sections.watch_out: The name writeFingerprint suggests writing, but it only records state, which can mislead a reader.

sections.name: writeFingerprint: if
sections.title: Scan demo coverage and export
sections.what: For the scan demo, checks the coverage notes on screen, sets a marker edit and chart settings, exports a PowerPoint file, unzips it, and checks the marker and coverage text. Then confirms the baseline is unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: exports must show the coverage notes and must not change the original demo.
sections.watch_out: The check reads exact text from the slide XML, so a change to slide wording breaks it.

summary: A read-only check, run against a running server, that the pinned LNG demos replay correctly and that nothing is written to the database during replay or export.
purpose: Confirms the guided demos show the agreed saved content, with coverage notes and clean hints, and that an export does not change the baseline.
why: Likely reason: demos are shown to people, so the test guards against stale or wrong content and against accidental database writes.
how: Records row counts and content hashes for several tables. Checks the pins, the project set and the evidence example, and checks hints and answers for banned values. For the scan demo, checks coverage notes on screen, applies a marker edit, exports a PowerPoint file, unzips it and checks the marker and coverage text. Then confirms the baseline is unchanged, a bad request returns 400, and the database snapshot matches the start.
inputs: The running API at the REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN address, the database, and the unzip command.
outputs: PASS lines and a no-writes line, or a failure. The temporary folder is removed at the end.
risks: Needs the server and database running, plus the unzip tool installed. The banned-value list is fixed.
debug: If the snapshot differs, something wrote to the database, so compare the counts and hashes. If a pin check fails, follow the message to the pin and re-measure it.
